quote: Most information about PAR activation and function derives from studies of a few proteases, for example thrombin in the case of PAR1, PAR3, and PAR4, and trypsin in the case of PAR2 and PAR4.
summary: Review of biased signaling by protease-activated receptors, with PAR1 discussed mainly as a thrombin receptor; no new data.

quote: APC elicits cytoprotective signaling through activation of protease activated receptor-1 (PAR1).
summary: Review of EPCR noting that activated protein C gives cytoprotective effects through PAR1, unlike the proinflammatory thrombin-PAR1 response.

quote: Similarly, synthetic receptor-activating peptides, corresponding to the exposed 'TL sequences' (e.g. SFLLRN-, for PAR1 or SLIGRL- for PAR2) can, like proteinase activation, also drive signalling via Gq , Gi and G12 /13 , without requiring receptor cleavage.
summary: Review on biased signalling of proteinase-activated receptors in inflammation, with PAR1 as one of four family members.

quote: In endotoxemia and sepsis, TF-dependent thrombin generation and activation of PAR1 on dendritic cells enhance inflammation.
summary: Review of tissue factor stating PAR1 activation on dendritic cells enhances inflammation in sepsis; no new data.

quote: Thrombin had no effect, suggesting absence of PAR-1, PAR-3, or PAR-4.
summary: Study of PAR-2 in pancreatic duct cells; PAR-1 is only inferred to be absent and not examined.
PAR2 agonist study in rat jejunum concluding a receptor distinct from PAR2 and PAR1 regulates transport; PAR1 only served as a pharmacological comparator.

quote: Cell-penetrating lipidated peptides called pepducins target specific intracellular loops of GPCRs and have recently emerged as effective allosteric modulators of GPCR activity.
summary: Pepducin minireview lists PAR1 among many GPCRs targeted; no PAR1-specific result for colitis.

quote: Intestinal irradiation up-regulates PAR-1 and causes a dose-dependent, sustained deficiency of microvascular TM that is independently associated with the severity of radiation toxicity.
summary: PAR-1 mRNA and protein rose in irradiated rat intestine alongside thrombomodulin loss; radiation enteropathy rather than colitis.

quote: In vitro, aPC inhibited glucose-induced expression of p66(Shc) mRNA and protein in podocytes (via PAR-1 and PAR-3) and various endothelial cell lines, but not in glomerular endothelial cells.
summary: Diabetic nephropathy paper where activated protein C acts via PAR-1 and PAR-3 in podocytes; no intestinal or colitis data.

quote: Most of these functions are manifested to APC binding to endothelial protein C receptor (EPCR) allowing PAR1 activation, but activation of other PARS is also implicated in some cases.
summary: Review of anti-inflammatory activated protein C signalling, which acts largely through EPCR-dependent PAR1 activation.

quote: Similarly, studies in vivo demonstrated that intracolonic infusion with PAR1 agonists increased colonic permeability in mice, and that this effect was abolished by pretreatment with a caspase-3 inhibitor.
summary: PAR1 agonists induced epithelial apoptosis and raised colonic permeability in cells and mice, suggesting PAR1 antagonists could protect the barrier.

quote: Genetic inactivation of CD11b, PAR1, or sphingosine kinase-1, but not EPCR, abolished the ability of APC to suppress the macrophage inflammatory response in vitro.
summary: PAR1 was needed for activated protein C to suppress macrophage inflammation, so PAR1 mediates an anti-inflammatory effect in endotoxemia.

quote: Colonic adenocarcinoma growth was reduced in PAR-1-deficient mice, implicating stromal cell-associated PAR-1 as one thrombin target important for tumor outgrowth.
summary: Stromal PAR-1 deficiency reduced colon tumor growth in mice; a cancer outcome, not colitis.

quote: Combined, but not individual, transfection with small interfering RNAs targeted against epithelial PAR-1 and -2, prevented the fall in TER induced by PMN contact.
summary: Knockdown of epithelial PAR-1 and PAR-2 prevented neutrophil-induced barrier loss and reduced transmigration; PAR-1 and -2 were increased in Crohn's colon.

quote: These effects were largely prevented by a specific PAR-1 antagonist and by short interfering RNA directed against PAR-1.
summary: PAR-1 antagonist or siRNA blocked elastase-induced apoptosis of human lung epithelial cells; lung injury setting, not intestinal.

quote: In wild-type but not PAR1(-/-) mice, TF-NH(2) stimulated Evans blue extravasation in the bladder, oesophagus, stomach, intestine and pancreas by 2 - 8 fold.
summary: PAR1 agonist drove plasma extravasation and oedema via sensory nerves in wild-type but not PAR1-knockout mice.
IBS paper in which F2R is only named as the parent of F2RL1/PAR2, the receptor actually studied.
B. fragilis toxin receptor study that excluded PAR1 to PAR4 as the receptor; PAR1 shows no role.

quote: PAR-1 and PAR-2 expression did not correlate to the pain sensation of PCa and CP patients.
summary: PAR-1 expression in pancreatic nerves did not correlate with pain in pancreatic cancer or chronic pancreatitis; not UC.

quote: PAR1 is the archetypal family member and has been the object of large-scale drug development programs since the 1990s.
summary: Review of PAR1-targeted therapeutics such as vorapaxar and drotrecogin-alfa and prospects for new PAR1 drugs; no colitis data.

quote: Among the novel genes discovered, WNT3, KANSL1, CRHR1, BOLA2, and GUCY1A3 are within a protein-protein interaction network with known PD genes.
summary: Cross-trait GWAS of Parkinson disease and autoimmune diseases including UC places GUCY1A3 among novel shared loci; no UC-specific effect or direction.

quote: We identified multiple metabolism-related genes machine learning genes (PDE4B, CDA, HMOX1, EHHADH, AMD1, GUCY1A1, GUCY1B1, UGCG, and FPGT).
summary: GUCY1A1 is one of nine machine-learning genes in lung transplant ischemia-reperfusion injury; no UC data.

quote: Here we show that MET is required for neutrophil chemoattraction and cytotoxicity in response to its ligand hepatocyte growth factor (HGF).
summary: Neutrophil Met deletion shows the HGF/MET axis drives neutrophil recruitment, including in colitis, and anti-tumour killing; HGF itself was not perturbed.

quote: Endogenous HGF is required for self-repair of injured livers, kidneys, lungs and so on.
summary: Review of HGF discovery describing its role in organ repair, protection and as a regenerative drug; no new data.

quote: Multiple antifibrotic factors, such as interleukin-10 (IL-10), interferon-γ (IFN-γ), bone morphogenetic protein-7 (BMP-7), hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) are also downregulated in CKD.
summary: Renal fibrosis review listing HGF as an antifibrotic factor downregulated in chronic kidney disease; no intestinal content.
